text: Titration can be used to determine the concentration of dissolved oxygen in samples of river water.
The procedure for the experiment is given.
step 1 Use five 50 cm graduated syringes, A, B, C, D and E, to collect five separate 30.0 cm
samples of river water.
step 2 In the laboratory, carefully add 5.0 cm of 0.220 mol dm manganese(II) sulfate,
MnSO (aq), into syringe A and mix well.
step 3 Add 5.0 cm of alkaline aqueous potassium iodide into syringe A and mix well.
step 4 Add 10.0 cm of dilute sulfuric acid into syringe A and mix well.
step 5 Transfer the contents of syringe A into a 150 cm conical flask. Rinse syringe A using
10 cm of distilled water and add washings to the conical flask.
step 6 Carry out one accurate titration of all the contents in the conical flask with 0.00200 mol dm
aqueous sodium thiosulfate, Na S O (aq), using starch indicator.
Repeat steps 2–6 for the samples in syringes B–E.

text: The activation energy, E , for the reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq), and aqueous
sodium thiosulfate, Na S O (aq), can be determined by an initial rates method.
2HCl(aq) + Na S O (aq) 2NaCl(aq) + H O(l) + S(s) + SO (g)
The solid sulfur formed is seen as a white suspension in the reaction mixture. The reactants are
mixed and the time, t, for a fixed quantity of sulfur to be formed is recorded.
A measure of the initial rate of the reaction is .
Standard solutions of 0.100 mol dm Na S O (aq) and 0.500 mol dm HCl(aq) are supplied.
Measurements are taken for a series of temperatures using the following procedure.
step 1 A thermostatically controlled water bath is set up.
step 2 A 100 cm conical flask is labelled A and a second 100 cm conical flask is labelled B.
step 3 10.00 cm of 0.100 mol dm Na S O (aq) is added to flask A. Flask A is placed in the
water bath.
step 4 10 cm of 0.500 mol dm HCl(aq) is added to flask B. Flask B is placed in the same
water bath.
step 5 Wait for 10 minutes.
step 6 Flask A is removed from the water bath and placed on a tile marked with a black cross.
step 7 The contents of flask B are added to flask A and a timer started.
step 8 The timer is stopped when the black cross is no longer visible. The time is recorded.
